rules.shared_rule: Distinguish calendar anchoring or a bounded calendar period from a recurrence rule. Use the function of the expression in context, not a weekday keyword alone.
rules.coexistence_rule: A recurrence can be anchored to a calendar period; distinct evidence can support both types.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Mondays and weekly receive both types across contexts; do not impose a global lexical mapping or claim exhaustive precedence.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish the calendar day or period from a part of a day. A combined expression may express both aspects.
rules.coexistence_rule: Tomorrow morning can separately express a date and a day part.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Tonight is annotated under either type; same-expression dual labelling or precedence requires a frozen annotation convention.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish a clock time, duration or offset from a named day part.
rules.coexistence_rule: A specified hour and its day part can both be present.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Night appears under both labels; broadening time to all temporal expressions would erase the intended boundary.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish a clock/duration expression from the standard or zone used to interpret a clock reading.
rules.coexistence_rule: Seven pm and PST support different types within one request.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Asking the time does not supply a clock value; a zone name does not imply an independently expressed time value.

rules.shared_rule: Use expressed performer/creator role as evidence for artist_name; a person's identity alone does not settle the dataset person-versus-artist convention.
rules.coexistence_rule: Different person references may serve different roles; absence of observed coannotation is not an exclusivity rule.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Artist names also occur in factoid contexts. Music topic alone cannot resolve all native assignments, nor establish person absence.

rules.shared_rule: Use an authorship relation to the referenced book as evidence for audiobook_author. Separate that relation from an ordinary personal reference.
rules.coexistence_rule: An author and another person can be mentioned together; no global exclusivity is justified.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Only four learning source utterances carry author annotations; same-span person/author precedence remains unverified.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish an identified business or organization from a location reference; a named business can also function as a destination.
rules.coexistence_rule: Business identity and geographic location can be separately expressed in the same request.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Walmart is assigned either label; venue role alone may not determine native annotation. Do not use capitalisation or brand lookup as a label rule.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish an area or surface treated as domestic activity space from a geographic location or destination.
rules.coexistence_rule: Separate domestic and geographic references may coexist; no coannotation in this population does not prove exclusivity.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Near-equivalent clean-the-floor requests receive different labels; this needs annotation adjudication, not an invented role distinction.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish a food or dish under discussion from a material explicitly serving as an input or substitute in preparation.
rules.coexistence_rule: Chicken used to make a dish or cream used to make butter can support separate ingredient and food expressions.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Rice in nearly equivalent cooking requests receives different labels; an input/output rule is a semantic candidate, not a complete reconstruction of native gold.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish a beverage reference from a material serving an ingredient role in preparation.
rules.coexistence_rule: Distinct expressions can name a beverage and one of its ingredients; shared substance identity does not imply mutual exclusion.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Water differs by context, while other preparation objects use food_type. Whole-ontology precedence needs review before negatives are inferred.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish the application or service providing access from the station or tuning reference being accessed.
rules.coexistence_rule: A station played through an application provides evidence for both roles.
rules.unresolved_constraint: A platform-only expression must not be assumed to contain a separately identified station; station existence still follows the type definition.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish software access from the organization or service providing a journey.
rules.coexistence_rule: A provider accessed via a separately named application can express both roles.
rules.unresolved_constraint: A service can also be an app. Uber labelled transport_agency does not establish app_name absence; native same-brand precedence remains unresolved.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish a property selecting music from an expression identifying a playlist collection.
rules.coexistence_rule: A descriptor and a playlist reference can coexist, including descriptive words within a playlist name under an admitted span policy.
rules.unresolved_constraint: Descriptive titles and genre words overlap; do not force one label from syntax or the presence of the word playlist alone.

rules.shared_rule: Distinguish an email-address identifying expression from a requested or stated personal-information field or attribute.
rules.coexistence_rule: A field name and its stated address can both be expressed.
rules.unresolved_constraint: A requested contact field need not include its value; conversely an address does not by itself express every possible contact-field type.
